column5: why=CASE and Singapore's competition authority warn that a website name suggesting Singapore does not necessarily mean the retailer is based here.

column3: Check marketplace payment protection and dispute rules before paying
column5: why=CASE recommends checking for seller authentication, escrow and clear dispute resolution, as well as the platform's return and refund terms.

column3: Check whether Lemon Law applies when buying used goods
column5: why=CASE says Singapore's Lemon Law covers second-hand consumer goods but not consumer-to-consumer sales; age and price matter when assessing quality.

column3: Compare water heater types and capacity for your household
column5: why=NEA says an instantaneous heater is generally more energy efficient than storage; storage capacity should fit household needs.

column3: Check the energy label assumptions when comparing water heaters
column5: why=NEA's label cost assumes three showers daily and an electricity cost of S$0.27 per kWh for electric heaters; actual costs vary.

column3: Check a storage water heater includes a pressure relief valve
column5: why=Singapore's Consumer Product Safety Office advises ensuring a storage water heater comes with a pressure relief valve.

column3: Budget for licensed electrical installation of a water heater
column5: why=Singapore's Consumer Product Safety Office says a licensed electrical worker should wire the heater directly to the mains via a double-pole switch, not an extension cord.

column3: Check the electric water heater's SAFETY Mark before purchase
column5: why=Singapore's Consumer Product Safety Office says instantaneous and storage electric heaters are controlled goods and their SAFETY Mark can be verified in its register.

column3: Vary fish choices and limit high-mercury predatory species
column5: why=SFA advises limiting swordfish, shark, king mackerel (batang), tilefish and bigeye tuna, while continuing to eat other fish as part of a balanced diet.

column3: Check the tuna species when comparing mercury guidance
column5: why=US FDA/EPA guidance for pregnancy and children classifies canned light tuna, albacore and bigeye differently because mercury levels vary by species.

column3: Chill fish promptly after shopping, especially tuna and mackerel
column5: why=SFA says histamine can form without proper refrigeration and is not destroyed by cooking once formed; it advises chilling fish promptly.

column3: Consider canned tuna in water or Healthier Choice sardines
column5: why=HealthHub suggests these canned fish as more affordable alternatives to expensive fish while providing valuable nutrients including omega-3 fats.

column3: Try a hair dryer's weight, balance and switches before buying
column5: why=CHOICE recommends holding the dryer and checking that its switches are comfortable and easy to operate.

column3: Look for separate heat and airflow controls on a hair dryer
column5: why=CHOICE says separate settings give more control over heat and air speed.

column3: Choose hair-dryer attachments for the style you actually use
column5: why=CHOICE describes concentrators as directing airflow for spot drying, while diffusers spread airflow for curly hair.

column3: Compare hair dryers by performance rather than price or buzzwords
column5: why=CHOICE reports some lower-priced dryers outperformed costly models and its tests did not show better performance from ionic, ceramic or tourmaline claims.

column3: Check hair straightener controls and heat adjustability
column5: why=CHOICE suggests checking control placement to avoid accidental shutoff and notes adjustable lower heat is useful for fine or damaged hair.

column3: Do not assume every flaky scalp needs medicated shampoo
column5: why=The American Academy of Dermatology says dry scalp and dandruff can look similar; persistent symptoms warrant a dermatologist's assessment.

column3: Measure the fridge opening and follow the maker's ventilation clearances
column5: why=NEA advises allowing space around a refrigerator for ventilation; insufficient clearance reduces cooling efficiency and increases energy use.

column3: Measure doorways and hallways before ordering a fridge
column5: why=CHOICE recommends checking the delivery route as well as the kitchen opening so the fridge can be brought into the home.

column3: Check fridge door swing and drawer clearance in your kitchen
column5: why=CHOICE recommends allowing room for doors and drawers to open and checking whether the hinge direction can be reversed if needed.

column3: Compare fridge layouts using the foods and containers you store
column5: why=CHOICE notes side-by-side compartments can be too narrow for wide items, while a French-door layout can accommodate wider platters.

column3: Check the fridge's shelves and crisper can be removed for cleaning
column5: why=CHOICE recommends checking shelf adjustment and removal and whether the crisper is easy to take out and clean.

column3: Compare fridge energy use as well as efficiency ticks
column5: why=NEA's energy label gives annual energy consumption and cost based on 24-hour operation and S$0.27 per kWh; actual costs vary.

column3: Try reaching bicycle brakes and shifters while holding the bars
column5: why=REI recommends checking grip while braking and shifting on a test ride; riders with smaller hands can ask about lever-reach adjustment.

column3: Inspect a used bicycle frame for cracks and serious dents
column5: why=Cycling UK recommends examining welds and stress points and seeking a bike-shop inspection if you lack the expertise.

column3: Ask for a used bicycle's proof of purchase and service history
column5: why=Cycling UK recommends asking about ownership documents, past crashes and servicing before buying a second-hand bike.

column3: Budget for a white front light and red rear light or reflector
column5: why=Singapore's LTA says bicycles used during hours of darkness must have a front white light and rear red light or reflector.

column3: Check e-bike accessories do not draw from the PAB electrical system
column5: why=LTA disallows added lights or electronic accessories drawing power from a power-assisted bicycle's electrical system.

column3: Try your air conditioner’s dry mode before buying a dehumidifier
column5: why=CHOICE says many air conditioners have a dry mode for mild cooling and dehumidification; a separate unit may help rooms without air conditioning.

column3: Compare dehumidifier extraction ratings at the same conditions
column5: why=CHOICE says rated water removal is often measured at 30°C and 80% relative humidity; performance changes with air conditions.

column3: Check a dehumidifier has a readable target-humidity setting
column5: why=CHOICE says a humidistat controls the target relative humidity, but unmarked rotary dials make the actual setting hard to identify.

column3: Check the dehumidifier tank is easy to remove and large enough
column5: why=CHOICE notes a small tank needs more frequent emptying; larger tanks are bulkier and it recommends an easily removed tank.

column3: Check continuous-drain compatibility for unattended dehumidifying
column5: why=CHOICE says a continuous drain is useful for long periods in one location; some models include an adaptor hose while others need one supplied.

column3: Listen to a dehumidifier before choosing it for a bedroom
column5: why=CHOICE says most units it measured exceed 50 dB and suggests listening to the unit because noise character matters too.

column3: Compare dehumidifier energy per litre removed, not wattage alone
column5: why=CHOICE notes a slower low-power unit can cost as much to remove 10 litres as a higher-power faster model.

column3: Compare microwave test performance rather than inverter claims alone
column5: why=CHOICE found some conventional models performed as well as inverter models in its microwave tests.

column3: Consider a flatbed microwave for awkwardly shaped dishes
column5: why=CHOICE says a flatbed has no rotating plate, giving more flexibility for dish shapes and making the interior easier to wipe.

column3: Compare robot vacuums on the floors and obstacles in your home
column5: why=CHOICE tests robots separately on hard floors and carpet, including crevices and edges, and checks avoidance of furniture and cables.

column3: Check how a robot mop refills and cleans its pads
column5: why=CHOICE says some robots need manual refills while others use a dock to refill water and wash dirty pads.

column3: Check replacement brushes and batteries are sold for a robot vacuum
column5: why=CHOICE lists the battery, brush bar, side brushes and filters among parts that should be replaceable.

column3: Check camera and privacy controls before buying a robot vacuum
column5: why=CHOICE suggests using no-go zones for sensitive areas on camera-equipped models, or choosing a model without a camera.

column3: Read the power mode behind a cordless vacuum runtime claim
column5: why=CHOICE says long claimed runtimes may use eco mode or a non-motorised tool; its tested maximum-power runtimes ranged from 6 to 33 minutes.

column3: Check cordless vacuum battery replacement and warranty separately
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some battery warranties are shorter than the cleaner warranty, and batteries eventually lose capacity.

column3: Check recurring bag costs on a self-emptying stick vacuum dock
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some self-emptying stick vacuums use disposable dust bags in their charging docks.

column3: Match blender type to the foods and batch size you make
column5: why=CHOICE says portable blenders have limited capacity and lack power for tasks such as grinding nuts or processing tough greens.

column3: Check blender test results for your intended task
column5: why=CHOICE tests smoothies and, for high-performance models, extra tasks including nut butter and sorbet; its overall ratings compare models of the same type.

column3: Check a blender jug and seal are easy to clean
column5: why=CHOICE says removable blades or a wider jug base can help cleaning, while lid seals may need to be removed for washing.

column3: Look for a blender lid lock and safety cut-out
column5: why=CHOICE advises checking for a safety cut-out time, lid lock and measuring cap lock to reduce blending accidents.

column3: Check a personal blender cup seals and unscrews easily
column5: why=CHOICE recommends checking the blade assembly has adequate grip and smooth threads that screw on firmly to prevent leaks.
